title: Finite-projective Hom-complex scalar extension
statement: Let A,B be commutative rings and phi:A -> B a ring homomorphism. Use the one-object ringed-site categories and normalized extension data d of [def-pc-perfect-rhom-base-change-map], including its pure-tensor equation on every Hom-complex product projection. Let P,Q be cochain complexes of A-module sheaves, with P bounded and with finite projective terms evaluated at the unique object. Then the chain map d.homMap(P,Q): B tensor_A Hom_A^\bullet(P,Q) -> Hom_B^\bullet(B tensor_A P,B tensor_A Q) is an isomorphism. No K-flatness of Q or flatness of B over A is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 0A6A, lemma-base-change-RHom, clause (1); bounded finite-projective representative argument

proof.text: At the unique object, sheaf scalar extension and sheaf internal Hom are ordinary scalar extension and module Hom. For P^p=A^r the canonical tensor-Hom map B tensor Hom_A(A^r,M) -> Hom_B(B^r,B tensor M) is the finite-coordinate isomorphism. For finite projective P^p, choose a splitting of it as a summand of A^r; extend the splitting to B and restrict the finite-coordinate map and its inverse to the corresponding Hom summands. This proves invertibility without any flatness assumption on B.

source.place: Lemma 0A6A, lemma-base-change-RHom, clause (1); bounded finite-projective representative argument

proof.text: In Hom(P,Q)^n, every factor outside the bounded interval for P is zero. The chosen infinite product therefore identifies with the finite product over that interval, and tensor distributes over this finite product. Compose this identification with the preceding finite-projective tensor-Hom isomorphisms. Its p-th product coordinate sends b tensor f, evaluated on c tensor x, to bc tensor f(x). The defining homMap_pure equation, generation by pure tensors, and joint injectivity of the product projections identify this degree map with (d.homMap P Q).f n.

source.place: Lemma 0A6A, lemma-base-change-RHom, clause (1); bounded finite-projective representative argument

proof.text: All degree components are isomorphisms. Inverting the chain-map equation shows their inverses commute with the differentials, so they assemble to the inverse chain map. Thus d.homMap P Q is an isomorphism.
